info.title: City4Christ API
info.description:
Auth foundation API. Use only test data on preview deployments. Interactive requests execute against this server and can create or change accounts. Public signup is closed by default. Email and Google availability depend on deployment configuration.

Keep access tokens in memory. Swagger Authorize accepts the access token only, without the Bearer prefix. Refresh cookies are HttpOnly and browser-managed; Swagger cannot manually set Cookie headers. This same-origin UI sends credentials automatically. Browser-origin checks still apply.

OTP: eight digits, ten minutes, five attempts, sixty-second resend cooldown. Limits: auth IP 60/min; register/resend 5 per account/15min; login 10 per account/15min; verify 20 per account/15min.

Groups: verified church members can discover church-audience groups. Only the Super Admin, Assistant Pastors, and assigned Ministry Leaders can discover the leadership-audience group. Membership and leadership permissions are enforced on every request.

get.description: Creates single-use state, nonce and PKCE S256 challenge. Sets a Secure, HttpOnly browser-binding cookie; SameSite follows the cross-site cookie configuration. Navigate to data.url in this browser; a fetch alone does not complete Google login. New signup obeys REGISTRATION_ENABLED. Google-only accounts have no local password. Optional returnTo enables browser completion: callback sets the refresh cookie and redirects to the stored frontend page, without access credentials in the URL or response body. The frontend then POSTs /auth/refresh with credentials. Binding cookie uses SameSite=None when cross-site cookies are enabled, otherwise Lax.

post.description: Requires an allowed Origin and an active Bearer session with password authentication or explicit confirmation within five minutes. Explicitly link Google to this account; email must match and be verified. Use /auth/reauthentication/password or /auth/reauthentication/google when confirmation is stale. Refreshing a token does not renew freshness. Existing sessions from before this migration and ordinary Google SSO without confirmation require confirmation. Optional returnTo enables browser completion: callback sets the refresh cookie and redirects to the stored frontend page, without access credentials in the URL or response body. The frontend then POSTs /auth/refresh with credentials. Binding cookie uses SameSite=None when cross-site cookies are enabled, otherwise Lax. Enrolled accounts additionally require fresh app-specific MFA confirmation; otherwise 403 mfa_required. Google linking checks this again at callback. Provider amr claims do not substitute for the application authenticator.

get.description: Google redirects here with code and state. Requires the matching browser-binding cookie and consumes the flow once. Validates signature, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce and verified email. Never automatically links matching local email: account_link_required means sign in locally and explicitly link. Returns JSON tokens and a refresh cookie, not a frontend redirect. A frontend completion page can subsequently call refresh using the cookie. The browser-binding cookie is cleared. Reauthentication-purpose flows confirm only an existing linked identity and existing active session. They require a recent signed auth_time, never issue or replace application tokens, and cannot be used as login/link flows.

Public metadata only. Sorted by publication time descending, then ID descending. Drafts (no publication timestamp) and future publications are hidden. Unknown or repeated query parameters and malformed cursors return 422. An empty catalog returns data: [] and nextCursor: "". Video links, when present, are canonical YouTube URLs. Editor writes use /admin/sermons; published series discovery is available at /api/v1/sermons/series; media hosting remains separate.

post.description: Requires a verified active Bearer session with an editor role from PostgreSQL, an allowed Origin and application/json. Always creates a draft; does not publish. Creation and actor/version audit are atomic. Mutations are limited to 60 per editor per minute. No role or publication state can be supplied here. Validation errors identify the field in error.fields. Response-only fields (id, publishedAt) are not accepted in request bodies.

patch.description: Requires an allowed Origin and current version. A stale version returns 409 without changing the sermon or audit. status=published publishes now and preserves the original publication date if already published. status=draft unpublishes immediately. status=scheduled requires future publishAt and hides the sermon until that instant. Each successful edit increments version and writes an audit event atomically. Role revocation applies without obtaining a new token. Omitted fields are preserved exactly; normalization applies only to supplied fields. Validation errors identify the field in error.fields. Response-only fields (id, publishedAt) are not accepted in request bodies.

get.description: Verified active Bearer session required. The caller may keep their own profile hidden and still browse visible members. Every page filters verified accounts with directoryVisible=true. Returns only id, firstName and lastName; no email, credentials, verification flags, roles or hidden-profile details. Search is literal, case-insensitive substring matching over firstName + space + lastName; % and _ are ordinary characters. Stable UUID ascending order, independent of names; pagination is live, not a frozen snapshot. 60 requests/account/minute and 120 requests/IP/minute. Unknown or repeated parameters are rejected. Opt out through PATCH /api/v1/me. No member detail-by-ID route is exposed.

post.description: Returns identical 202 responses for eligible, unknown, unverified, Google-only and cooldown accounts. Five requests per normalized email per 15 minutes, plus shared 60 auth requests per IP per minute. One-minute resend cooldown. Resending invalidates the previous link. Password accounts must already have verified email. Requesting a reset does not revoke sessions. Links expire in 15 minutes; token is carried in the frontend URL fragment. Requires allowed Origin and JSON body.

post.description: Consumes a single-use emailed token, replaces the Argon2id hash and revokes all existing sessions atomically. Ten attempts per token per 15 minutes plus shared IP limit. Invalid, expired and used tokens return invalid_reset_token. Clears the refresh cookie and queues a password-change notification. Sign in normally afterwards; Google-only accounts cannot acquire a password through recovery. Requires allowed Origin and JSON body.

get.description: Verified active Bearer session required. Uses the authenticated account only; query parameters are rejected. Returns supported assignments and exact scoped capabilities from one PostgreSQL snapshot; committed grants/revocations are reflected without replacing the JWT. No automatic promotions, new church-role grants or authorization bypass. Existing own-profile and directory access do not require a staff role. Maximum 60 requests/account/minute and 120/IP/minute. Refresh navigation on page entry, focus or explicit user action; every protected server action still authorizes independently.

post.description: Verified active Bearer session required. Query parameters and target account identifiers are rejected. Confirmation does not grant any role or satisfy MFA. Allowed Origin and application/json required. Password and Google confirmation share five attempts/account/15 minutes; auth IP limit is 60/minute. Failures return no secrets. Requests nonce, PKCE S256, one-use state, max_age=0 and essential signed auth_time. Browser binding cookie is Secure and HttpOnly. The existing Google callback validates the already-linked subject and recent auth_time; it never signs up, links an identity or starts a session. Missing/stale auth_time fails closed. Browser completion returns to stored returnTo with reauthentication=complete or auth_error=reauthentication_failed; markers are display hints, not proof. Read status after return. Without returnTo, callback returns a status object. No additional Google redirect URI is needed.

post.description: Verified active Bearer session. roles.read permits Super Admin, Assistant Pastor and Staff lookup. Limits shared across church-role routes: 30/account/minute and 120/IP/minute. Responses are no-store. Unknown or duplicate query parameters are rejected. Every mutation additionally requires fresh primary identity confirmation and mandatory current-session application MFA, rechecked in the assignment transaction after locks. Super Admin alone can grant/revoke the four global church roles; Assistant Pastor/Staff can appoint registered-scope ministry leaders only. Protected-role grant targets must be verified and MFA-enrolled. No self-grant; only Super Admin self-resignation is allowed when another verified MFA-enrolled Super Admin remains. Changes and audit commit atomically. Confirm identity/MFA then explicitly resubmit; never automatically replay a mutation. This route does not bootstrap administrators or create ministries.
